title: HF4360 (2017-2018 Regular): Criminal background checks for pistol transfers required, transfers excepted, petitions to prohibit people from possessing firearms allowed, transfer of semiautomatic military-style assault weapons and large-capacity magazines prohibited, buyback program established, slide-fire stock clarified as a trigger activator, criminal penalties provided, and money appropriated.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/90/2018/0/HF/4360/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version (no date on file; 2018 session). Two articles. Article 1 strikes old transfer-permit exception numbering and repeals Minn. Stat. 609.66 subd. 1f and 624.7132 subd. 14. Article 2 amends 624.713 subd. 1 to add a bar for people under an extreme risk protection order, and creates 624.7171 to 624.7178 (petition, hearing, emergency orders, firearm transfer and return, offenses, liability protection). Dollar amounts are blank. Section 3 defines 'large-capacity magazine' (section 624.712, subd. 13); the definition is not quoted here.

operative_text:
Article 1, Section 5 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): (1) each transfer occurring in whole or in part in the state shall be preceded by a background check on the transferee; and
Article 1, Section 5 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3): Where both parties to a prospective transfer are unlicensed persons, the transferor and transferee shall appear jointly before a federally licensed firearms dealer with the pistol and request that the federally licensed firearms dealer conduct a background check on the transferee and facilitate the transfer.
Article 1, Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 609.66, subd. 1i): (2) for a second or subsequent conviction, is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than two years or to payment of a fine of not more than $5,000, or both.
Article 1, Section 6 (Minn. Stat. 624.7135, subd. 2): It is unlawful to transfer a semiautomatic military-style assault weapon.
Article 1, Section 7 (Minn. Stat. 624.7136, subd. 2): It is unlawful to transfer a large-capacity magazine.
Article 1, Section 8 (voluntary buyback): The commissioner of public safety shall create a voluntary semiautomatic military-style assault weapon and large-capacity magazine buyback program.
Article 1, Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 609.67, subd. 1): "Trigger activator" means a removable manual or power driven trigger activating device constructed and designed so that, when attached to a firearm, the rate at which the trigger may be pulled increases and the rate of fire of the firearm increases to approximate that of a machine gun.
Article 2, Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7172): (d) If the court finds there is a preponderance of the evidence to issue an extreme risk protection order, the court shall issue the order prohibiting the person from possessing a firearm for the duration of the order.
Article 2, Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7172): (e) The order shall have a fixed period, to be determined by the court, of not less than six months and not more than two years, subject to renewal or extension under section 624.7173.
Article 2, Section 6 (Minn. Stat. 624.7175): (a) Upon issuance of an extreme risk protection order, the court shall direct the respondent to transfer immediately any firearms the person possesses, within 24 hours, to a federally licensed firearms dealer, a law enforcement agency, or third party.
